performance_tasks.brief: Water access: instrument and community storage — supplied enquiry and own-investigation transfer. A1 Identify [1]: Identify the enquiry population from the supplied water-access survey; A1 Design [5]: Design five usable questionnaire elements for the stated enquiry, with neutral wording and recordable responses; A1 Describe [4]: Carry out systematic selection from the stated household list after a suitable start; A1 Explain [2]: Explain how consent and privacy are protected in this non-sensitive survey; A1 Suggest [3]: Repair the specific pilot wording difficulty and explain the improvement; A1 Calculate [2]: Calculate a survey proportion or difference from supplied counts; A1 Draw [4]: Construct a suitable bar chart from the original categorical counts; A1 Describe [4]: Use the chart and source evidence to describe the water-access pattern; A2 State [2]: State two feasible aims for a small community water-storage activity; A2 Describe [3]: Organise volunteers, permissions and responsibilities for that activity; A2 Suggest [2]: Propose feasible funding linked to the stated cost/resources; A2 Explain [3]: Match one implementation obstacle to a practical response and responsible implementer; B State [2]: State the actual topic/area and linked aim; B Explain [2]: Explain what the pilot revealed and the revision actually made; B Describe [4]: Describe the collection procedure actually used; B Describe [4]: Support the enquiry findings with evidence and explain their implication; B Suggest [3]: A feasible recommendation with an implementer tied to those findings Supply original self-contained figures and sources. Each AO split is a planner judgement, not an official rubric. Sections A1/A2 sum to 35 and B to 15. Use a clearly fictional worked enquiry and then transfer B to the learner’s actual investigation; do not fabricate their fieldwork.

Each AO split is a planner judgement, not an official rubric. Sections A1/A2 sum to 35 and B to 15. ao_mix_note: The syllabus states its AO weights as a share of MARKS, so planned_ao_mix_by_marks is the one that answers "does this resource match the exam". It values each card at the tariff of the question it models, split across the AOs the card declares, and values each performance task at the marks of the paper part it models. The count-based mix below is reported only because it is what a reader expects to see; do not balance against it. AO shares by ITEM COUNT: Every objective needs one recall anchor, so AO1 has a structural floor of about 56% in this topic (36 objectives against 64 slots) and cannot reach the None% target by count however many other cards are added - padding the bank to chase it makes the resource worse. The framework already measures the AO4 share in practice time rather than by count for the same reason. Treat AO1 above target as expected, and AO2/AO3/AO4 below target as the thing worth fixing.
